bull.t: Accelerating platform growth and customer expansion
bull.b: Strong consumption growth, expanding large-account spend and high retention indicate that Snowflake is deepening its role in customer data infrastructure, supporting durable revenue growth through broader workloads and increased usage within existing accounts.

bull.t: AI adoption and strategic ecosystem expansion
bull.b: Rapid adoption of native AI products can expand Snowflake’s addressable workloads and drive incremental platform consumption. Expanded AWS and OpenAI relationships also strengthen distribution, ecosystem reach and the platform’s strategic relevance.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and improving operating discipline
bull.b: Positive and improving cash generation provides funding for product investment and strategic initiatives while reducing reliance on external capital. Margin expansion and raised operating-margin guidance suggest operating leverage is beginning to develop as scale increases.

bear.t: Persistent GAAP losses and high operating expense intensity
bear.b: Snowflake’s attractive gross economics have not yet translated into GAAP profitability. Continued operating expense intensity limits earnings resilience, complicates long-term profit conversion and leaves results more dependent on sustained growth and expense discipline.

bear.t: Rising leverage alongside negative returns on equity
bear.b: The shift toward a more debt-heavy capital structure reduces financial flexibility while losses persist. Although the balance sheet is not described as distressed, higher leverage combined with deeply negative ROE increases execution and funding risk.

AI growth may not create equivalent profit growth if inference and infrastructure costs remain elevated. Customer throttling could also limit consumption expansion, making future monetization depend on cost efficiencies and sustained willingness to deploy usage-heavy workloads.
